title: Islanded manifest orchestration and image bundle playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for islanded (air-gapped / isolated network) site installs and upgrades. It focuses on: deterministic manifest layout, curated image + dependency bundles, transport strategies (sneakernet, signed media, portable registries), and a concise Terraform module interface for mirrors/seed registries. The doc is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight — aim is to capture an operational runbook and the minimal TF surface we need to keep private deployments reproducible and auditable.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, Platform Engineers, Solutions Eng on private deployments
- Scope: bootstrap install, periodic upgrades, emergency rollback, and validation testing for islanded sites (no egress). Not a full security policy — assumes customer has their own KMS/CA procedures.

High-level constraints and goals:
- Deterministic bundle layout. Every bundle produced by our build pipeline must include a top-level manifest (manifest.yaml) with SHA256 checksums and signature metadata.
- Signed artifacts. All tarball images and manifest files must be signed using a customer-managed signing key (KMS/HSM) or an operator signing key for customers without KMS.
- Minimal TF surface. One Terraform module that describes where artifacts live (mirror_bucket / registry_prefix), how to seed the local registry, and a verification hook.
- Upgrade safety. Canary nodes + staged rollout with automated validation gates.
- Offline validation. Include a local test harness (containerized) that can perform smoke inference, checksum validation, and image signature verification without network access.

Terminology (quick):
- bundle: tar.gz package containing images, charts, manifests, and optional host packages
- manifest.yaml: canonical index listing file paths, sha256sum, signed_by, and model_version mapping
- seed-registry: small container registry run in-cluster used to load images from bundle media
- transport: physical or air-gap method (sneakernet, secure HDD courier, internal upload via controlled bastion)

Bundle layout (recommended):
- /manifest.yaml  # canonical index (see sample below)
- /images/registry-mirror.tar  # OCI mirror generated by `ctr images export` or `skopeo sync` output
- /charts/redwood-platform-<semver>.tgz
- /models/<model-name>/<version>.tar.gz  # model artifacts, keys stripped if necessary
- /checksums/manifest.sha256  # sha256(manifest.yaml) - signed separately
- /signatures/manifest.sig  # detached signature (PSS or ECDSA)
- /docs/install-steps.txt

Sample manifest.yaml (human readable canonical):
# NOTE: this is an expository example; real manifests must be generated by pipeline
site_id: islanded-demo-2024
bundle_id: rwinf-bundle-2024-11-03
created_at: 2024-11-03T14:22:00Z
artifacts:
  - path: images/registry-mirror.tar
    sha256: <hex>
    type: oci-mirror
    signed_by: redwood-operator-key-1
  - path: charts/redwood-platform-1.6.2.tgz
    sha256: <hex>
    type: helm-chart
    signed_by: redwood-operator-key-1
  - path: models/llama-3b/2024-10-12.tar.gz
    sha256: <hex>
    type: model-artifact
    model_version: 2024-10-12
    signed_by: customer-kms-key

Signatures and verification:
- Signing approach: pipeline produces detached signatures for manifest.yaml and for each artifact checksum. Prefer customer-managed KMS HSM. If customer cannot bring KMS, create an operator signing key with strict access and rotate per-release.
- Verification step: before import on the islanded site, run `verify-bundle --manifest manifest.yaml --public-keys /keys` which performs: sha256 checks on all listed files, verifies detached signatures, and ensures mapping of model_version to allowed versions list.

Transport options and constraints:
1) Sneakernet (physical media)
   - Best for highly restricted customers with no bastion.
   - Use tamper-evident sealed drives. Attach manifest + signed checksums + signature along with transport chain of custody doc.
   - Bring-forward step: on arrival, compute checksums on an isolated machine, verify, then copy into the site staging bucket.
2) Bastion-assisted upload
   - Customer provides an upload bastion host that can receive the bundle from courier but not permit arbitrary egress.
   - Uploads must be done over SCP/SFTP over a customer-controlled bastion; checksums verified by the service account.
3) Pre-populated registry appliance (portable)
   - A small disk appliance bootstrapped with a seed-registry image. Operator plugs into site network and performs `registry seed import` locally.

Terraform module interface (minimal surface)
Purpose: provide a single module that declares how the bundle will be referenced in customer infra and a verification hook that runs after TF apply to ensure the bundle is present and validated. Keep plumbing minimal so downstream consumers can implement site-specific secrets management.
Module inputs (recommended):
- name: string  # logical name for the bundle
- mirror_bucket: string  # optional (gs:// or s3://) location used by our pipeline to stage bundle for transfer
- registry_prefix: string  # e.g., local-registry.example.com/redwood
- manifest_path: string  # path within mirror_bucket to manifest.yaml
- signature_key_id: string  # identifier for public verification key in KMS/secret manager
- validation_command: string  # optional command to run post-apply (containerized)
- keep_last: number  # how many bundles to retain on disk (default 3)
Outputs:
- seed_job_id: string
- verification_status: string  # SIMPLE: OK | FAIL

Terraform best-practices notes:
- Module must be idempotent for repeated applies with same bundle_id. Avoid forcing re-import unless bundle_id changes.
- Provide a local-exec null_resource hook that runs the `verify-bundle` container after apply - but gate it behind a boolean input so operators can opt out.
- Use object locking or versioned prefixes for mirror_bucket to avoid accidental overwrites.

Image registry seed operator (runtime behavior):
- A single CRD `ImageSeed` references manifest.yaml and a local storage location.
- Behavior: when ImageSeed created, operator spawns a Job that:
  1) extracts registry-mirror.tar into a temporary registry (skopeo/registry:2 approach)
  2) re-tags images to local registry_prefix and pushes them into local registry
  3) updates a ConfigMap with imported image list and checksums
- Operator must run as a restricted account and log signed verification of each pushed image (sha + signed artifact reference).

Upgrade plan (staged):
1) Preflight (offsite)
   - Produce bundle and manifest, run offline verification harness, run sample inference tests against a CI runner preloaded with the bundle (mirror image import into ephemeral registry).
   - Create release notes entry with exact bundle_id and list of images/models. Attach signatures and checksums.
2) Transport + ingestion (site)
   - Ingest bundle into staging bucket or local path. Run `verify-bundle`. Run smoke checks (container image pull + helm template dry-run).
3) Seed registry + dry-run deploy
   - Use seed operator to import images into local registry with `--dry-run` to populate registry metadata only.
   - Apply Helm charts with `--set imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent --dry-run` then perform manifest-level reverse-lookup tests (ensure each Deployment has image present in registry metadata).
4) Canary rollout (2-3 nodes)
   - Mark 2 nodes as canary. Deploy platform components for canaries only. Run automated local validation tests: health probes, 1-min latency check, smoke inference sample across 3 model sizes.
   - Wait minimum 30 minutes and validate logs for errors.
5) Progressive rollout
   - Increase to 25% of nodes, run 1-hour validation, then to 70% for 2 hours. Monitor errors and objective comparisons (latency p95, cost proxies).
6) Full rollout or rollback
   - If validation checks pass, proceed to full rollout. If not, use recorded previous bundle_id to trigger rollback path in TF module (re-create ImageSeed pointing to previous bundle and re-run).

Validation tests (local offline harness):
- verify-bundle: checksums + detached sigs + manifest schema
- smoke-infer: run 3 small prompt/trace tests against each model type (text gen, chat, embedding)
- kv-cache test: start a simple service that warms KV cache and verifies cache hits after restart
- storage-integrity: confirm model files decompress and produce expected sample hash
- helm-dryrun-assert: verifies rendered manifests reference images that exist in local registry metadata

Rollback and emergency procedures:
- Keep last 3 bundles retained and tagged via TF module `keep_last`.
- Emergency revert: if critical, run `tf apply` with `bundle_id = previous` and set `force_reseed=true`. Then restart affected pods with `kubectl rollout restart`.
- If registry corruption suspected: stop registry, snapshot storage, trigger re-import from signed bundle using a dedicated import job that validates image checksums before pushing.

Monitoring and observability requirements:
- Seed operator logs must be shipped to local aggregators with a signed ingestion event (timestamp, bundle_id, artifact_sha).
- Post-upgrade, collect the following for 72 hours: p50/p95 latency, error rate, model-not-found errors, image-pull failures. Attach these metrics to the upgrade ticket.

Security and compliance notes:
- Private key material MUST NOT be included in bundles. Only signatures and public verification keys are allowed.
- Document chain-of-custody for each transport and keep an immutable record (signed PDF) stored with the bundle manifest.

Troubleshooting checklist (quick):
- verify-bundle fails signature check -> re-run sign step, confirm public key ID and timestamp, check clock drift on site host.
- seed operator fails when pushing -> inspect registry storage permissions, check disk pressure, verify registry_prefix DNS/resolution in-cluster.
- helm install failing due to image pull errors -> verify image tags exist in registry metadata ConfigMap and check that `imagePullSecrets` are applied.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should the TF module include a local tiny registry appliance deployment or leave registry as a customer-provided component? (Tradeoff: convenience vs policy surface)
- Signing strategy for model artifacts vs container images: do we require distinct signing keys?
- KMS onboarding flow: how do we automate verification of customer public keys for signing without exposing private material?

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Priya: prototype `verify-bundle` container and push basic CLI to github (due 2024-12-01)
- Evan: draft minimal Terraform module interface and example usage (due 2024-12-08)
- Kaitlyn: design canary validation test harness (containerized) and smoke test suite (due 2024-12-15)
- Diego: run a table-top transport exercise with ops to simulate sneakernet chain-of-custody (due 2024-12-10)

Notes / references:
- See linked artifacts for current PR and ticket.
- Keep this doc as the short operational playbook; move canonical spec to Confluence after we've validated the prototype.

Version history:
- 2024-11-03: initial draft (Priya)
- 2024-11-18: added TF interface notes (Evan)
- 2024-12-02: added verification harness checklist (Kaitlyn)
- 2025-01-20: added staged rollout timings and canary guidance (Priya)

---
Notes to self: document should remain terse and action oriented. Avoid embedding long sample scripts here; link to github snippets instead once PRs land.
